head: claude/mi154-export-exit-head-family-flag-20260906
title: MI-154: export_exit_head.py — let the family token be DECLARED, not only derived
body:
## The next bug in the exit-head chain, found before anyone hit it

Split out of the MI-154 findings PR (companion). **Measured 2026-09-06**, not hypothesised.

`scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py` stamped `"family": fam_dir.name` with **no override**, so the token an artifact carries is whatever the training round happened to name its output directory. That is fine while the directory name and the consuming unit's declared family are the same word, and it breaks the moment they are not.

**They are not.** The surviving E0 scalp rounds on the trainer are laid out **per leg** — `runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/scalp_5m_20260814T151003Z/` holds `ict_scalp_sol_5m/`, `ict_scalp_xrp_5m/` and `ict_scalp_avax_5m/` — so the DERIVED token is `ict_scalp_sol_5m`. The `ict_scalp` consumer added by PR #11140 declares `family="ict_scalp"` and accepts:

```python
_ACCEPTED_FAMILIES = {
    "donchian":  {"donchian", "trend_donchian"},
    "ict_scalp": {"ict_scalp", "scalp"},
}
```

`ict_scalp_sol_5m` is in neither set. So a scalp exit head exported the obvious way would be published, loaded, and then **REFUSED** — loudly (that guard logs a WARNING, which is good design) but scoring nothing. Whoever does the export after #11140 lands would hit this and have to work backwards from a live WARNING.

## The fix

`--family` declares the token. **Omitting it is byte-for-byte the legacy derivation**, so no existing round moves and no published artifact changes:

```python
family       = a.family if a.family else fam_dir.name
family_basis = "declared" if a.family else "derived_from_dir"
```

The CLI line now states which basis was used, so a mismatch is diagnosable at **export** time rather than only from a live WARNING hours later on another box — the diagnostic-provenance rule that the output must state what it actually computed.

⚠️ **No new artifact FIELD was added, deliberately.** Stamping `family_basis` into the JSON would be a key nothing reads — the exact "written and never read" class MI-154's companion PR files a backlog row about. It would be incoherent to fix that class by adding an instance of it.

## Tests

`tests/test_export_exit_head_family_token.py` — 5 assertions, including:

- a **positive control** that the script exists at all, without which every source-parsing assertion below it would pass vacuously on a renamed file;
- that the **old unconditional stamp is gone** — without this, `--family` would be accepted and then silently ignored, which is worse than not offering the flag;
- that omitting `--family` still reproduces `fam_dir.name`.

**17 passed** alongside the pre-existing `tests/test_exit_head_training_window.py`, so the exporter's existing behaviour is unregressed.

## Landing — and why this is a separate PR

`.github/pr-landing/mi154-export-exit-head-family-flag-20260906.json` → **tier 1 / `hold`**; `pr-landing: OK — state=declared_hold`. Not armed for auto-merge.

`pr-landing-guard`'s `TIER1_SURFACE` allowlist lists `scripts/ci/**`, `scripts/ops/**`, `scripts/research/**` and `scripts/reports/**` but **not** `scripts/ml/**`, so it declines to certify self-landing here. That is the guard working as designed — fail-closed on a path it cannot vouch for — and narrowing the companion PR is its own first-listed remedy, so the findings land autonomously instead of waiting behind a one-line flag.

`tier: 1` is the accurate tier: `CLAUDE.md`'s tier table calls *tooling* Tier-1 and `docs/claude/trainer-vm-mode.md` makes trainer work autonomous. **The hold is about the guard's allowlist, not about the tier** — I have not re-declared it as Tier-2/3 work, because it is not, and over-declaring to satisfy a vocabulary would make the record less true rather than more cautious.

**What this asks for:** one manager/operator read of a single trainer-side file. It touches no `src/`, no `config/`, no order path; the script is not imported by any live runtime path, and the artifact it writes is gated by stage.
